\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{உரிமம்} (urimam)}{உரிமம் (urimam)}]{\ta{உரிமம்} (urimam) — a licence; a permit}

\label{lesson:TA-C407-urimam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to run out, then the Tamil for to wear down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{உரிமம்}}
\textbf{\ta{உரிமம்}} — \emph{urimam} — \textquotedblleft{}a licence; a permit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{ஓட்டுநர்} \ta{உரிமம்} \ta{இல்லாமல்} \ta{கார்} \ta{ஓட்டக்} \ta{கூடாது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ōṭṭunar urimam illāmal kār ōṭṭak kūṭātu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
You must not drive a car without a driving licence.
\end{quote}

\ta{ஓட்டுநர்} \ta{உரிமம்} is a driving licence.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{உரிமம்}} (\emph{urimam}) is native Dravidian, a modern coinage built on the root of \ta{உரிமை}, \textquotedblleft{}a right, ownership\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 654), with the noun ending \emph{-am} in place of \emph{-mai}: a right given on paper.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{urimam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{urimam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōṭṭunar urimam illāmal kār ōṭṭak kūṭātu.} — You must not drive a car without a driving licence.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to run out, then the Tamil for to wear down, then say \emph{urimam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{உரிமம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A licence; a permit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{கிலோமீட்டர்} (kilōmīṭṭar)}{கிலோமீட்டர் (kilōmīṭṭar)}]{\ta{கிலோமீட்டர்} (kilōmīṭṭar) — a kilometre}

\label{lesson:TA-C407-kilomittar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to wear down, then the Tamil for a licence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{கிலோமீட்டர்}}
\textbf{\ta{கிலோமீட்டர்}} — \emph{kilōmīṭṭar} — \textquotedblleft{}a kilometre\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{எங்கள்} \ta{ஊர்} \ta{இங்கிருந்து} \ta{இருபது} \ta{கிலோமீட்டர்} \ta{தூரம்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṅkaḷ ūr iṅkiruntu irupatu kilōmīṭṭar tūram.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our town is twenty kilometres from here.
\end{quote}

Numbers come before it without a plural: \ta{இருபது} \ta{கிலோமீட்டர்}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{கிலோமீட்டர்}} (\emph{kilōmīṭṭar}) is a loan from English \emph{kilometre}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kilōmīṭṭar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kilōmīṭṭar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṅkaḷ ūr iṅkiruntu irupatu kilōmīṭṭar tūram.} — Our town is twenty kilometres from here.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to wear down, then the Tamil for a licence, then say \emph{kilōmīṭṭar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{கிலோமீட்டர்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A kilometre\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{மைல்கல்} (mailkal)}{மைல்கல் (mailkal)}]{\ta{மைல்கல்} (mailkal) — a milestone}

\label{lesson:TA-C407-mailkal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a licence, then the Tamil for a kilometre.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மைல்கல்}}
\textbf{\ta{மைல்கல்}} — \emph{mailkal} — \textquotedblleft{}a milestone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{சாலையோரத்தில்} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{பழைய} \ta{மைல்கல்} \ta{இருக்கிறது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cālaiyōrattil oru paḻaiya mailkal irukkiṟatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is an old milestone at the side of the road.
\end{quote}

It also means a turning point: \ta{வாழ்க்கையில்} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{மைல்கல்}, a milestone in life.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{மைல்கல்}} (\emph{mailkal}) is built from a loan from English \emph{mile} and native \ta{கல்}, \textquotedblleft{}a stone\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1298).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mailkal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mailkal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cālaiyōrattil oru paḻaiya mailkal irukkiṟatu.} — There is an old milestone at the side of the road.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a licence, then the Tamil for a kilometre, then say \emph{mailkal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{மைல்கல்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A milestone\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{வழித்தடம்} (vaḻittaṭam)}{வழித்தடம் (vaḻittaṭam)}]{\ta{வழித்தடம்} (vaḻittaṭam) — a route}

\label{lesson:TA-C407-valittatam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a kilometre, then the Tamil for a milestone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வழித்தடம்}}
\textbf{\ta{வழித்தடம்}} — \emph{vaḻittaṭam} — \textquotedblleft{}a route\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{இந்தப்} \ta{பேருந்தின்} \ta{வழித்தடம்} \ta{மாறியிருக்கிறது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intap pēruntiṉ vaḻittaṭam māṟiyirukkiṟatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This bus's route has changed.
\end{quote}

\ta{தடம்} alone is a track or a footprint; \ta{வழி} doubles the \ta{த்}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{வழித்தடம்}} (\emph{vaḻittaṭam}) is built from \ta{வழி}, \textquotedblleft{}a way\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5297), and \ta{தடம்}, \textquotedblleft{}a path, a route\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3024).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaḻittaṭam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaḻittaṭam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intap pēruntiṉ vaḻittaṭam māṟiyirukkiṟatu.} — This bus's route has changed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a kilometre, then the Tamil for a milestone, then say \emph{vaḻittaṭam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{வழித்தடம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A route\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{ஓரங்கட்டு} (ōraṅkaṭṭu)}{ஓரங்கட்டு (ōraṅkaṭṭu)}]{\ta{ஓரங்கட்டு} (ōraṅkaṭṭu) — to pull over; to sideline}

\label{lesson:TA-C407-orankattu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a milestone, then the Tamil for a route.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஓரங்கட்டு}}
\textbf{\ta{ஓரங்கட்டு}} — \emph{ōraṅkaṭṭu} — \textquotedblleft{}to pull over; to sideline\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{காவலர்} \ta{சொன்னதால்} \ta{நான்} \ta{காரை} \ta{ஓரங்கட்டினேன்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāvalar coṉṉatāl nāṉ kārai ōraṅkaṭṭiṉēṉ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because the policeman told me to, I pulled the car over.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{ஓரங்கட்டினேன்}, \emph{ōraṅkaṭṭiṉēṉ}.

\ta{ஓரம்}, the edge, + \ta{கட்டு}: to put to one side.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{ஓரங்கட்டு}} (\emph{ōraṅkaṭṭu}) is built from \ta{ஓரம்}, \textquotedblleft{}an edge, a side\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1060), and \ta{கட்டு}, \textquotedblleft{}to tie, to fix\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1147).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōraṅkaṭṭu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōraṅkaṭṭu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāvalar coṉṉatāl nāṉ kārai ōraṅkaṭṭiṉēṉ.} — Because the policeman told me to, I pulled the car over.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a milestone, then the Tamil for a route, then say \emph{ōraṅkaṭṭu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{ஓரங்கட்டு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pull over; to sideline\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Getting around, first pass}

\label{lesson:TA-R407-review-400-407}



\begin{quote}
Say the Tamil for a platform and a railway track.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a platform, a railway track, arrival, to postpone, to switch
  \item a bus conductor, a bus stop, to jolt, to stagger, a ride
  \item luggage, a suitcase, a sack, to carry, to unload
  \item a highway, a flyover, a detour, a junction, to speed
  \item a motor vehicle, a lorry, a scooter, to overtake, to collide
  \item a taxi, a metro, to connect, a lounge, an interval
  \item fuel, petrol, a tyre, to run out, to wear down
  \item a licence, a kilometre, a milestone, a route, to pull over
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A platform? (\textbf{\ta{நடைமேடை}}, \emph{naṭaimēṭai}.) A railway track? (\textbf{\ta{தண்டவாளம்}}, \emph{taṇṭavāḷam}.) Arrival? (\textbf{\ta{வருகை}}, \emph{varukai}.) To postpone? (\textbf{\ta{ஒத்திவை}}, \emph{ottivai}.) To switch? (\textbf{\ta{மாறு}}, \emph{māṟu}.) A bus conductor? (\textbf{\ta{நடத்துநர்}}, \emph{naṭattunar}.) A bus stop? (\textbf{\ta{நிறுத்தம்}}, \emph{niṟuttam}.) To jolt? (\textbf{\ta{குலுங்கு}}, \emph{kuluṅku}.) To stagger? (\textbf{\ta{தள்ளாடு}}, \emph{taḷḷāṭu}.) A ride? (\textbf{\ta{சவாரி}}, \emph{cavāri}.) Luggage? (\textbf{\ta{சாமான்}}, \emph{cāmāṉ}.) A suitcase? (\textbf{\ta{சூட்கேஸ்}}, \emph{cūṭkēs}.) A sack? (\textbf{\ta{மூட்டை}}, \emph{mūṭṭai}.) To carry? (\textbf{\ta{சும}}, \emph{cuma}.) To unload? (\textbf{\ta{இறக்கு}}, \emph{iṟakku}.) A highway? (\textbf{\ta{நெடுஞ்சாலை}}, \emph{neṭuñcālai}.) A flyover? (\textbf{\ta{மேம்பாலம்}}, \emph{mēmpālam}.) A detour? (\textbf{\ta{சுற்றுவழி}}, \emph{cuṟṟuvaḻi}.) A junction? (\textbf{\ta{சந்திப்பு}}, \emph{cantippu}.) To speed? (\textbf{\ta{விரை}}, \emph{virai}.) A motor vehicle? (\textbf{\ta{வாகனம்}}, \emph{vākaṉam}.) A lorry? (\textbf{\ta{லாரி}}, \emph{lāri}.) A scooter? (\textbf{\ta{ஸ்கூட்டர்}}, \emph{skūṭṭar}.) To overtake? (\textbf{\ta{முந்து}}, \emph{muntu}.) To collide? (\textbf{\ta{மோது}}, \emph{mōtu}.) A taxi? (\textbf{\ta{டாக்ஸி}}, \emph{ṭāksi}.) A metro? (\textbf{\ta{மெட்ரோ}}, \emph{meṭrō}.) To connect? (\textbf{\ta{இணை}}, \emph{iṇai}.) A lounge? (\textbf{\ta{ஓய்வறை}}, \emph{ōyvaṟai}.) An interval? (\textbf{\ta{இடைவேளை}}, \emph{iṭaivēḷai}.) Fuel? (\textbf{\ta{எரிபொருள்}}, \emph{eriporuḷ}.) Petrol? (\textbf{\ta{பெட்ரோல்}}, \emph{peṭrōl}.) A tyre? (\textbf{\ta{டயர்}}, \emph{ṭayar}.) To run out? (\textbf{\ta{தீர்}}, \emph{tīr}.) To wear down? (\textbf{\ta{தேய்}}, \emph{tēy}.) A licence? (\textbf{\ta{உரிமம்}}, \emph{urimam}.) A kilometre? (\textbf{\ta{கிலோமீட்டர்}}, \emph{kilōmīṭṭar}.) A milestone? (\textbf{\ta{மைல்கல்}}, \emph{mailkal}.) A route? (\textbf{\ta{வழித்தடம்}}, \emph{vaḻittaṭam}.) To pull over? (\textbf{\ta{ஓரங்கட்டு}}, \emph{ōraṅkaṭṭu}.)
